item.title: Devlog #1 for Secrets of Bastille
item.description:
Been making some progress on Demo 2! Was going to re-do the dungeon system for the MZ version but I decided to make it work in Demo 2 and have a page open for it on RPG Maker Web.

I am working with ChatGPT to help create some plugins while I do the code review with the UI. I am aiming for a Dragon Quest/Mystery Dungeon style UI as you can see in the screenshot below

item.title: Learning the Tic80
item.description:
I’m back with another update and this time I’m leaning into the Tic-80 Fantasy Console.

I really like how you can use multiple languages but I ended up going to stick with Lua incase I want to work on projects in Pico-8 or try Love2D again.

I also like how it’s open-source and essentially free with a pro version so I can experiment with no issues. Other features I like is more resolution and able to use keyboard/mouse (point and click adventure games anyone?), as well as addtional players and controller buttons.

item.title: Mini March Update
item.description:
Been pretty busy this month so far! I been working some new projects and almost done tidying up my first Commodore 64 homebrew made entirely using Basic. I have some ideas to push more into it but I think it’s okay. It’s playable now but I’m waiting on Chat GPT to come up with some cool cover art for it.

https://github.com/DjKniteX/MirageWars/

Some upcoming projects for the sake of retro programing is that I would like to only work with stuff that can be cross-developed, using tools and games that can be made on multiple OSs. I will be doing stuff with tic-80 and very soon, Eldiron.

item.title: My First Hugo Post
item.description:
Welcome to my first Hugo post. I am testing out some new stuff and hoping to code my blog from scratch so I can have more freedom.

One thing I would like to say is that there will be ADs enabled through Google Sense. Now I like to use ad blockers so I will not tell you to use it or not. I only enabled this to generate earnings and I know it won’t be much but at least it’s something. So if you are reading this without an ad blocker awesome, if not, don’t worry too much about it.

item.title: Welcome to NSXplus!
item.description:
Hello everyone! Welcome to NSXplus! Named with my initials and my (future) love of the MSX computers. I am rebranding to do a lot of retro coding which I hope to dev log and open up a youtube channel as well, something along the lines of LGR and 8bitguy but more towards coding 8bit games.

It’s still in early stages but I would try to blog all things retro tech as well as my cybersecurity journey. Which on the other hand, have gotten to an okay start where I volunteered to do some website testing where I attempted to do an SQL injection and ran Burp Suite to find cookie vulnerabilities. So far so good on that end.

item.title: March update
item.description:
Hey guys, will be working on some cool stuff later this year after I set up my new workstation.

As of right now, I am learning Evennia, self-teaching myself computer science, and learning Basic C64 and Assembly language.

Working on a drug wars type game for the C64 using BASIC. It’ll be called Mirage Wars and it still a work in progress. Hoping to push it out later this month. planning on buying a controller and a flash cart for my c64 soon to test it out on actual hardware

item.title: Back to the grind
item.description:
I began my passion projects. With a lot of down time at work I was able to get my coding environment up and running for C, C++, C#, Python, and Assembly.

I am currently learning 6502/6510 Assembly and looking to make quick roms for both the C64 and NES for learning before I dig into them completely.

I am going to be learning C# to work with Monogame and experiment with that.

item.title: Passion Projects
item.description:
Okay it’s been awhile and I haven’t gotten around to work on my WGU article but I am now officially, Nikki X, M.S.

I would like to work towards CISSP but first I want to try to get into academia by parting a part time adjunct faculty teaching intro comp sci classes.

I been working on slide decks and doing research in this field and would like to start writing essays on my topic which I will self-published here. It will most likely be simple APA essays while I work towards my goals.

item.title: WGU MSCSIA: Week 23: Another Class Down! (D485 Tips)
item.description:
I got the results for D485 about a day after I submitted and passed it first try! A lot of folks seems to hate this class and I will say that the PA was kind of tedious but overall it was not that bad especially since I was unfamiliar with Azure Cloud and was able to learn as I go.

I forgot where I saw it but if you are about to take D485 - Cloud Security, I would say try to find the PA template as it gives you tips/notes on what they expect and it helped a lot with writing the PA. I knew what to look for, a hint on where it would be, and screenshots of what needs to be done. The books that they had you read was pretty good, I’m going to pick up a hard copy. The book is called: Cloud security handbook: Find out how to effectively secure cloud environments using AWS, Azure, and GCP which you can grab on Amazon here: https://www.amazon.com/Cloud-Security-Handbook-effectively- environments/dp/180056919X/ref=sr_1_1?crid=1DT7UX66TA05K&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.q8wRh- XPeMlnkSYYQ7JEwA.NuGZnT9gFIV07nSi0B67M_igq_5nuvMLD0Uh80hxyho&dib_tag=se&keywords=Cloud+security+handbook%3A+Find+out+how+to+effectively+secure+cloud+environments+using+AWS%2C+Azure%2C+and+GCP&qid=1741757547&sprefix=cloud+security+handbook+find+out+how+to+effectively+secure+cloud+environments+using+aws%2C+azure%2C+and+gcp%2Caps%2C386&sr=8-1

item.title: WGU MSCSIA: Week 19 - Pentest+ Passed!
item.description:
Big news…

I passed the Pentest+ with a score of 761 which I did 10 points better than CySa+. It was a little bit harder but the labs were probably the best part.

Now it’s time for the other big news…. I got laid off so I’m going to be job hunting as soon as I get back from London and enjoy a little bit of me time.

I am working on D485, which is Cloud Security. Thankfully it’s mainly a Lab with a paper assessment so I’ll be focusing my free time on this. Last course for the term!

item.title: WGU MSCSIA: Week 18 - Paper Assessment done, time for the exam.
item.description:
Got the passing mark for my paper assessment with no fixes/amends I needed to do and now I’m off to focusing most of my school time on Pentest+

I am currently taking Dion’s practice exams and casually reading through the sybex book. I finished Dion’s PT0-002 notes and been going through the tryhackme’s module for Pentest+

I’m getting comfortable good scores and knowing what I miss when casually doing the exams. (I finish them in 20 minutes or less). I’ll take extra time when doing the actual exam. I usually spend about 45 minutes answering first then doing the PBQs then use the remaining time to double check my answers.

item.title: WGU MSCSIA: Week 17 - Cram Time
item.description:
Just cramming for Pentest+ and spending most of my free time working on labs and studying. I am almost done with the Paper Assessment for D484 and it’s pretty straightforward once I figured out what I wanted to write and gather my sources.

I might tend to overthink things but once I’m in the zone I am locked in.

Hoping to turn it in for review in a couple of days and if I need to revise hoping to get that done by the end of the weekend so I can focus mainly on Pentesting.

item.title: WGU MSCSIA - Week 7: CySA+ Time
item.description: Just wrapped up Week 7 and finished the Paper Assignment. It wasn’t that bad. I was expecting an essay but it was pretty straightforward. It did got sent back because I misread one of the columns. The virtual lab that you had to do for the Paper Assignment was a bit confusing cause it doesn’t label what you need to go to so you’ll have to do some cyber sleuthing which I believe is a skill that everyone should master.

item.title: WGU MSCSIA Week 6: Security Operations and CySA+ Crunch Time
item.description: Another week has gone by and I was able to finish D486 GRC first try! No comment from me except to just follow the rubric. I am not trying to finish a class in a day or in a week because I would like to retain the information I’m learning. When I started this paper, I would try to do a section per day (at least outlining) and then when I feel like it’s good to go, then I have a go at it and write to my heart’s content.

item.title: WGU MSCSIA Week 5: Beginning of November
item.description:
It’s the beginning of November and I just submitted my paper for D486! I’m about 50/50 on it and I’m sure I’ll get it returned to fix something only because the rubric for was very ambiguous. I think I know what they want but I will see what happens after they review it.

I’m pulling through D482 especially the certmaster lessons. I been going through them on my spare time at work and work on the practice quizzes when I can. The labs are pretty good as they provide hands on experience with tools and software that I normally don’t use at work. There is a paper assignment for this course as well but it doesn’t look too bad. It looks like you fill out the a form regarding the lab you took. I only just saw a glimpse of it so I’m not 100% sure until I actually tackle it. I’m hoping to take the CySa+ exam before Thanksgiving (Or earlier!) and get the next course started by the end of November too. (Or early December!)

item.title: WGU MSCSIA Week 4: Almost the end of the 1st month.
item.description:
It’s almost the end of October and I’m about to wrap up my 2nd class. I’m still working through the PA and I’m hoping to get it done by October 31st. I started it last week but took a couple days break to hit up some concerts in Los Angeles and San Jose.

This paper had more research I needed to do but once I got the materials I needed, it’ll be a breeze! (I needed to look at impact rating standards). I also have to find sources supporting the rating and how to deal with them as well for D486. But now that I know how the assessments are done, my tip is to write with the rubric. If it tells you to list 3 things, list those 3 things. No less and no more.

item.title: WGU MSCSIA Week 3: Passed D482!
item.description:
Week 3 has finished and got the email this morning that I passed D482!

I did have to do a revision and thankfully it was all minor. I only had to fix some things in 2 parts but considering that I haven’t done any paper essays in about a decade I didn’t feel bad at all.For anyone reading. For anyone reading and getting ready to start the course, I would recommend to double check your work and make sure you follow what the rubric needs. Don’t over think it too much. Try to start writing what you want to write, templating your essay and then start on it.

item.title: WGU MSCSIA - Week 2: Beginning my 2nd class!
item.description:
Week 2 was a breeze. I started my 2nd course which I ended up doing D486 Governance since it’s another paper assessment course. I am listening/watching CySA+ videos while I’m doing the labs and course material to get a head start which I’m hoping to commit to CySA+ by the end of October and be certified in early November!

I’m almost done with the paper assessment for D482 and I did a lot of research to make sure I was on the right track. Been looking at reddit for tips but now that I started writing the paper, it’s all coming together. I might have been overthinking it or it could be because I haven’t been doing anything school related in over a decade. I had to look up how to write an essay and what APA sources were!

item.title: I'm an ISC2 Member now.
item.description: I took and passed my test on the same day (July 15) and received my certificate the next day. 50$ a year isn’t that bad especially since the program makes you get CPE (continue education) to keep your certificates. I like this approach because I feel like many people earn certs and when they don’t get a job they just let it sit there and they are not doing anything to level up or keep up with the trend.

item.title: I'm a graduate student now.. I think
item.description:

But I’m officially been admitted to WGU’s Master Program for Cybersecurity and Information Assurance. (referring to this program as MSCSIA from now on).

I have my (ISC)2 CC exam scheduled for next week and if I pass I hope I can use that to take one less class which means one less exam so I can finish way earlier.

item.title: Another Summer Jam
item.description:
It’s Intern Season, so expect to see many interns on campus! Life is looking good, weather is being nice and all in all I’m proud of what I been able to achieve this year.

I sent in my application to attend WGU for their Masters program for Cybersecurity unfortunately I am not qualified for Fafsa. I was able to submit my certification to see what can be transferred over so I’m thinking if I can buckle down I can complete the program in 6 months and take a 5k hit. or 1 year and it be just shy of 10k. Which isn’t too bad considering I’ll be getting a Masters degree + certifications. I think I can do it in 6 months but I’ll definitely be able to do it one year.

item.title: June Post
item.description:
Finally, a new post!

I’m able to get some time to sit down and blog something again with some news. I passed the CompTIA Security+ exam with 761 pts! It was close but I managed to pull through. I almost used up my time as well. I think I was just under 10 minutes when I finished and I’ll tell you it was a tough one.

With this certificate, I learned new skills and now I have something to add to my resume to make it stand out more. Now my next step is to fast track to Network+ so when I do have to renew my Sec+ I would have Network+ renewed as well.

item.title: A Long March
item.description:
Hello everyone! I’m back at relearning Python/Django and been doing a udemy course! As I mentioned before, this will help me work with Evennia a lot better/easier and will give me a leg up in Cyber Security since a lot of scripting is mostly done in Python.

After getting more comfortable with Python, I would like to learn and use pygame for game jams moving forward (with the occasional Pico8). I’m hoping to begin using python/pygame for the 2024 Version!

item.title: February Update
item.description:
Hello everyone, been working on setting up my server now that I gotten it and have gotten a good stream of regular users playing. My electricity went up 100% though but I moved to a newer place where it’s cheaper so I’m able to spare a few bucks.

Hollowgrounds is still on pause but I am doing the world building during my free time while learning BASIC and 6502 Assembly.

item.title: It's been awhile
item.description:
Sorry I been MIA! I have a lot to catch up but I spent the holidays relaxing and moving to my new apartment!

I been gearing up for what I’m going to present later this year with multiple projects that I been working on. I finished laying out my novel and hoping to begin writing that this year and finish it sometime next year or after.

My dream projects are now part of the same Mythos that share similarities but not directly related. Somewhat similar to the Ivalice Alliance. They’re share some stuff but not everything.

item.title: GO23 - Pre Blog
item.description:
Hey guys, taking a 95% pause on HG right now to focus on Game Off 2023! I didn’t get to do it last year since we did the multiplayer summer jam one but this time we are going in full force!

This year we will be learning Godot and turning this project into a text- adventure game that takes place in Space with the theme of Scales.

The game will obviously be open source and so the game will be titled: The Tales of Three Scales.

item.title: HG Log #6: End of October
item.description:
Hey everyone, sorry it’s been awhile but I have been busy this month. I interviewed for an internal project, I returned from Sacramento from Judging Pokemon Regionals and now I’m getting some time in to work on personal projects before Game Jam November!

I was able to get some work done for Hollowgrounds. I finished the basic template map for the 2nd area and after I tidy some of this up I will begin working on the 4 quests that will be featured in the Beta that will happen later this year early next!

item.title: HG Log #5 / Busy Week
item.description: Hey guys, it’s been awhile but October has been pretty busy so far. Catching up with school and working towards landing a 6 month project to do Mobile App Testing so I been preparing for that. Not much details about this project just yet since my Manager presented the short term project to us recently so I will find out soon. I know we have to interview for it and I saw the prep and it looks somewhat easy with a minor things that I’m familiar with but not enough to go into details so I will work on that.

item.title: HG Log #4
item.description:
Hello October 1st! It’s been awhile since we worked on this but now that time is freeing up, this month will be a little busy as we finished the template of the Beta maps, only thing left is to make it pretty!

we have finished templating the first village, the training caves, nearby areas that takes you to the first cave/tunnel that will take you to the 2nd village available in the Prologue.

item.title: HG Devlog #3 - Mapping
item.description:
Hey guys, A small update as in there probably be less development time this week due to studying and I’m seeing a concert and just going to relax from the pc every once in awhile but I’ll still blog. But once the weekend hits I’ll be doing more work.

I finished Baldur’s Gate 3 and it’s a sweet game. Thinking of playing it again in the Winter. But I’m currently setting up my Wii to run retroarch on my CRT TV (13’ Toshiba TV with a built in DVD-Player) to play some old classic RPGS to get some inspirations in terms of storylines, mapping, and art inspirations.

item.title: Slow week
item.description: Nothing much to say. Just been a slow week getting back into the groove of things since I got back from vacation. I am currently learning how to do pixel art and been on the drawing boards for the MUD which I will announce soon. Will give you the engine that I am working on which is MirageMUD. This MUD will follow the structure of Ember Online but will take place in Space.

item.title: History of the Gaiuss Trilogy (Cartuga, Gralina, and now Hollowgrounds)
item.description:
Not a dev log but just a quick history of the game series and why I want to make this the way it is now.

At the time of this writing, Hollowground is the current work in project with many other projects I have on the pipeline, which also includes the Cartuga - Definitive Edition. I was able to find the original source, thankfully I had it up on my Github so I will take a look, rebalance it, add some new stuff and re-release it.

item.title: Gralina/HG - Dev Log #2
item.description: If you guys are wondering what the HG stands for in the title, it’s the name of the game now. So moving forward, Hollowgrounds is the name of the main game where Gralina will be the first Episode/Chapter of the game. With the 2nd Episode, being an expansion. I’m expecting the dev lifespan at the rate that we are going is at least a year and a half. Server will be up until someone beats the game and then after that the server will be up for at least another year or until the server dies (if I decided to get like a 3 year server plan, etc)

item.title: Gralina - DEV LOG #1
item.description: Hello everyone, welcome to my first Dev Log. A written one at that because I feel like I can probably write what I want instead of freestyling on the top of my head. Anyways, I wanted to let you guys know that I brought Gralina back from the dead. Originally a RPG Maker MV game as a sequel to my class-project, Cartuga, I decided to turn this one into an online game.

item.title: Hello World... From Byond!
item.description: Before I get right to it, I just wanted to announce that I proably be closing my original blog that I had running for almost a decade at https://djknitex.wordpress.com. It’s seen better days and now that I’m more focused on my professional career than my non-existent esports and music career. I might as well pivot over here. Needless to say, I will continue blogging but I will be more active on this one.

item.title: The Start of September
item.description: It’s August 31st. The end of August and I have to say that I have relearned a lot of stuff in terms of programming but I’m happy to pick up where I left off. I have decided to enroll into Calbright College since it’s free for students in California for their Cyber Security program where we can learn and obtain CompTIA Security+ Certificate, which is an industry standard. My goal with this program is to add this to my portfolio and level up in my career.

item.title: Byond Programming!
item.description:
So I began learning how to program DM, Dream Maker (The Language Byond uses) and its been very fun. I have seen this a very long time ago and wasn’t very appealing at the time haha.

Byond stands for Build Your Own Net Dream and that’s what I’m going to do. I began going through some documentation and watching a few videos to get a hang of things and I think I’ll be comfortable enough with it by the end of the year to publish something. I will most likely use this for Game Jam 2023.

item.title: End of the Month
item.description:
I am currently taking a work vacation in LA from the Bay and decided to work on my personal projects in the mean time. Since I was young I always wanted to build a game in VB6 since at the time every body was coding and making games using VB (and similar languages) at least for the games I was following.

During the weekend I decided to look at Byond because that was one of the few instances where I stumbled upon code (especially source code). I took at a look at the documentation and then I realized how much of a “legacy” language it was and how I should add it to my portfolio for nostalgia reasons.

item.title: Python3
item.description: Back with another blog post. Right now, I am currently learning Django with a course I bought from Udemy. I figured since Evennia has their webapp side of things built with Django, I might as well learn how Django works if I wanted to make changes to the website. This is also an excuse to learn more Python in depth rather than just working on the mud with it so yeah. It’ll be a win win situation.

item.title: Summer Jams
item.description:
I got out and dusted off a spare Macbook Pro I had which I am now using to get back into djing and doing gigs. I also brought it out so I can work on my projects on a better environment. I actually would have used Ubuntu but I needed a system where I can do both djing and programming on the side.

Not much news here but with the MUD being built with Evennia, I decided that my first web rpg is going to be done in Django so my python knowledge will overlap.

item.title: New Year, New Me
item.description:
I’m back at it again and hopefully I’ll be more active. At least once a month! Anyways a quick update going into this new year is that I’m finally up in Silicon Valley. I’ve always wanted to live here for the longest time and it feels so surreal haha. Maybe I’ll start vlogging again.

I’m currently liking my new job and I have taken the time to re-learn Go (the game) and picking up backgammon. I haven’t done a whole lot in the city just yet but I plan on joining various meetup groups.

item.title: Multiplayer Game Jam 2022
item.description:
Nothing too huge but I’m putting together a team with some of the folks over at mockinbird.dev to compete in our next Game Jam this fall!

https://itch.io/jam/back-to-school-multiplayer-game-jam-2022

Some of our teammates have experience with Unity but not with Photon so this will be interesting. I’ll most likely be taking over creative design and initial code as I am also learning C#/Unity on the side with BASIC/ASM6502.

So far so good.

item.title: Some tech news!
item.description:
I just started a new role and getting my foot wet in the Cyber Security world! I’ll be auditing code making sure there are up to date and nothing is wrong (Hopefully no body sticking in hidden crypto miners in their code)

I’m currently still onboarding/training but the company sounds really good to work with so I’m hoping to learn more in the mean time.

I started learning Assembly and C64 Basic again so I’m hoping to punch out some cool homebrew with some real hardware soon! I have tons of resources that I’m going through so I’m hoping to knock some text adventure games out.

item.title: New Game Jam submission and future Python learning
item.description:
Our first game under the mockinbird.dev has been released for NaNoRenO 2022! Link here: https://djknitex.itch.io/echoes-that-sing.

Aside from that, I know it’s going to be a small post but I started re- learning Python as well as SQL to be able to get on track to become a Junior Data Scientist at my current company. So I’m on the grind and will report back with other Python related things I will be doing (Or web dev!)

item.title: Look Out! Dev Blog #1
item.description:
We been at this for a couple of weeks taking on as Lead Developer and defactor scrum master. Would like to introduce old collaborator Matthew again while taking on new Audio Engineer, Quintin (Longtime member of Team SKYNITE) to add music/sounds for us.

So we decided to use rot.js to make a roguelike based game within the bugs theme using a boilerplate by chr15m and its been working wonders while adding some of our own new features in. We have about one week to finish before we go on Holiday mode then its QA and bug mashing after that. Hopefully we can take top 100 this time! Our last year submission didn’t do too hot but the one before we made it to top 75!

item.title: Game Off 2021 is a go!
item.description:

Our meeting in Gather;

Our team is a go! We are now recruiting Quintin to help work on sound/audio design so our game will have “professionally” made music and sounds!

The theme for this year’s Game Off 2021 is Bugs and as we plan from our first meeting we have a direction that we want to take.

Nothing concrete for now but please feel free to follow along as I post more updates. November is going to be busy!

item.title: About
item.description: Hey Guys. My name is Nikki X and I do a lot of things. By trade I’m a web developer but at night I’m doing many different things. I am a competitive card game player (Poker, Bridge, Pokemon and Digimon TCG), amateur competitive Starcraft player. I love making music. I still DJ on the side. I work on a Game Jam team. I also like cooking. I sometimes stream RE7 and in the future will do RE8 and Dying Light speedruns.

item.title: My new blog
item.description:
Decided to make a new blog again. Keeping up with HexoJS was tiresome and very hard to make a backup for (At least for me.) so I decided to go with Blogger, which has then been very easy to setup and I used them for my other projects as well.

I know there’s nothing now but if you like to see my oldest posts feel free to fork them from my Github.
